Cinde Warmington

Democratic candidate for Governor, New Hampshire · Challenger

Attorney and health care advocate; former New Hampshire Executive Councilor

Cinde Warmington is a Democrat and a former New Hampshire Executive Councilor. She ran for governor in 2024 and lost the Democratic primary to Joyce Craig. She filed for governor again on June 4, 2026, won the Democratic nomination in the September 8, 2026 primary, and faces Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte and Libertarian Stephen Villee in the general election.

Where Warmington stands

Education Freedom Accounts / school vouchers
Opposes the Education Freedom Account voucher program. Says taxpayer money should go to public schools, and argues the voucher expansion has pushed local property taxes up.
Property taxes and school funding
Says the state is diverting public school money to vouchers, which leaves towns to raise more through property taxes to fund their schools.
Business taxes
Said in the October 20, 2026 debate that she would not support new taxes on New Hampshire businesses under current economic conditions.
Data centers and energy costs
Calls for an immediate moratorium on AI data centers in New Hampshire. Says this would protect against rising electric rates and allow environmental impact studies.
Renewable energy / net metering
Supports rules that encourage private investment in renewable energy, including solar projects up to 5 megawatts where feasible, to lower energy costs (2024 campaign site).
Abortion
Supports writing protections for access to legal abortion and contraception into state law. Opposes bans in the first and second trimesters.
Housing
Says rising property taxes make it hard for seniors to stay in their homes and that they have few places to downsize to. Calls for more housing supply.
Federal policy / Trump administration
Argues that Trump administration tariffs and federal funding cuts have hurt New Hampshire's economy, and says Gov. Ayotte has not pushed back enough.

Background

  • New Hampshire Executive Councilor, District 2 (2021–2025)
  • Candidate for governor, 2024 (lost Democratic primary)
  • Democratic nominee for governor, 2026 (unopposed in the September 8, 2026 primary per NH Bulletin)
  • Former partner, Shaheen & Gordon law firm
  • Attorney; describes herself as a lifelong health care advocate
